title: Chapter 12: Things to Consider About Per-Share Earnings; Zweig commentary

claims.text: Do not annualize one quarter or accept a headline EPS figure before checking dilution and special charges; alternative definitions can produce materially different apparent valuation multiples.

Repeated business closures, contract losses and restructuring costs cannot disappear from economic earnings simply by being called special items. Reconcile when costs were recognized and when cash is paid.
claims.anchor: include only its profitable contracts and operations

claims.text: Separate sustainable taxed earning power from the finite value of loss-related tax benefits, and account for contingent dilution when valuing each common share.

A multiyear earnings history should include special losses and gains and show recent figures alongside averages. Averages can reduce cycle noise but cannot cure changed business economics or inconsistent accounting.
claims.anchor: They should be included in the average earnings

claims.text: Compare accounting policies across years and peers, including revenue recognition, capitalization, inventories and pension assumptions. Changes and nonrecurring labels prompt investigation rather than an automatic accusation.
claims.anchor: all mean that you need to investigate further

claims.text: Reject automatic dismissal of every pro forma figure; use a complete bridge to reported results and preserve excluded real costs. The source itself describes legitimate uses before its categorical instruction.
claims.anchor: the only thing you should do

assimilation: Carry defined, reconciled per-share earnings inputs into valuation. Preserve actual charges, dilution assumptions and the finite life of special tax benefits. Use a multi-period view without laundering inconvenient losses out of the average. When allocation of a charge is unknown, record the uncertainty rather than invent a precise normalized figure.
adversarial_review: The ALCOA example explicitly admits that true normalized 1970 earnings cannot be determined from the supplied disclosure. A finite pension return cannot be certified from a selected historical decade or Buffett's reputation. PDF 303 says $1.4 billion is 13% of $7.2 billion, an arithmetic inconsistency; do not ingest that percentage. Recognizing revenue before installment cash collection is not automatically improper: performance and collectibility matter. Capitalization is also not inherently abusive. Table 12-1 assigns three-fifths of a special charge as an illustrative compromise, not an observed economic allocation. No historical accounting or tax treatment is asserted as a current rule.
memory_delta: Require EPS-definition and cash-flow reconciliation, including charges, tax benefits and dilution. Treat unknown normalization as an uncertainty interval, and test accounting-policy changes against business substance and comparable firms.
reading_provenance: Read all PDF pages 289-305 and inspected table 12-1 and figure 12-1, including the special-charge allocation footnote and repeated inventory write-downs.
